additions.reason: Gadlut (controlled greatness/deliberate pride) is the dominant node of Package 1. The Rebbe teaches it is equivalent in function and nature to a fast — both produce forgetting of previous wisdom as a gateway to higher comprehension. This is the central concept of the Torah and is entirely absent from the dataset.

additions.reason: Fasting is the other node of Package 1's core bechina pair. The Rebbe uses Rabbi Zeira's fast (to forget the Babylonian Talmud so as to ascend to the higher level of Torat Eretz Yisrael) as the paradigm case that defines the essential nature of gadlut. Both gadlut and ta'anit share the mechanism of causing forgetting-of-prior-wisdom. This node does appear in the dataset in other Torahs but has no bechina edge for Torah #246.
additions.source_quote: כִּי כְּשֶׁצָּרִיךְ לָבוֹא לְהַשָּׂגָה וְלַעֲלוֹת לְאֵיזֶה מַדְרֵגָה, אֲזַי צָרִיךְ לִשְׁכֹּחַ אֶת חָכְמָתוֹ שֶׁמִּקֹּדֶם... רַבִּי זֵירָא הִתְעַנָּה כְּדֵי לִשְׁכֹּחַ תַּלְמוּד בַּבְלִי

additions.reason: Genuine pride (gaavah) is the evil counterpart to Package 1's gadlut. Where gadlut is controlled and used as a spiritual tool, gaavah is the uncontrolled reality of pride — and the Rebbe states it is identical in nature to becoming a fool. It causes wisdom to depart completely. The Talmudic statement 'כָּל הַמִּתְגָּאֶה חָכְמָתוֹ מִסְתַּלֶּקֶת מִמֶּנּוּ' is its defining bechina.
additions.source_quote: כִּי בְּוַדַּאי גַּדְלוּת הוּא אִסּוּר גָּדוֹל מְאֹד, וְאִם יִתְגָּאֶה בֶּאֱמֶת, בְּוַדַּאי חָכְמָתוֹ תִּסְתַּלֵּק מִמֶּנּוּ לְגַמְרֵי

additions.reason: The fool (shote) is the other node of Package 2's bechina pair with gaavah. The Rebbe states that if one genuinely becomes proud, one will become 'שׁוֹטֶה מַמָּשׁ' — an actual fool. This is not merely a consequence (eitza) but a statement of shared nature: genuine pride IS foolishness. Both gaavah and shote are two expressions of the person whose wisdom has been completely extinguished.
additions.source_quote: וְלֹא יָבוֹא לְהַשָּׂגָה, וְיִהְיֶה נַעֲשֶׂה שׁוֹטֶה מַמָּשׁ

additions.reason: Forgetting of previous wisdom is the shared mechanism and essence of both gadlut and ta'anit in this Torah. It is not merely a result (eitza) but the defining quality that makes them bechinas of each other. 'כִּי עַל־יְדֵי הַגַּדְלוּת שׁוֹכֵחַ גַּם כֵּן אֶת חָכְמָתוֹ' — through gadlut one also forgets one's wisdom. This concept functions as the common denominator of Package 1 and warrants its own node.
additions.source_quote: כִּי עַל־יְדֵי הַגַּדְלוּת שׁוֹכֵחַ גַּם כֵּן אֶת חָכְמָתוֹ

additions.reason: Attainment/comprehension (hashagah) is the goal toward which gadlut-as-ta'anit is directed. While this is primarily an eitza relationship (gadlut leads to hashagah), the Torah frames the entire necessity of gadlut around it: one needs gadlut in order to reach hashagah. The specific mention of 'Torat Eretz Yisrael' as a higher hashagah versus Talmud Bavli as the lower one gives this concept depth. It is absent from the dataset for Torah #246.

analysis_notes.note_on_dataset_gap: Torah #246 is entirely uncharted in torahData.js. The reference numbers in the dataset jump from 245 to 247, meaning no edges of any type (bechina or eitza) exist for this Torah. All analysis above is based exclusively on source-text reading. The Torah is short (two dense paragraphs) but conceptually rich, centering on a single bold bechina (gadlut = ta'anit) and its dangerous evil mirror (gaavah = shote).
analysis_notes.note_on_good_evil_mirror: The good/evil mirror structure is exceptionally tight in Torah #246. Package 1 (gadlut = ta'anit, controlled, 'לִבּוֹ בְּדַרְכֵי ה׳') and Package 2 (gaavah = shote, uncontrolled, 'הַמִּתְגָּאֶה') are the SAME phenomenon at two poles. The Rebbe is teaching that the exact same act (raising oneself) is either a holy spiritual technique or a catastrophic sin — depending entirely on the intention and art (amanut) behind it.
